title: Check dropper-post function
summary: Inspect the dropper post, cycle it through its travel and verify predictable remote operation without disassembling the post.

steps.title: Inspect the post and saddle
steps.instruction: Check the exposed post, saddle connection and visible frame interface for damage, heavy contamination or obvious looseness.
steps.why: A functional test should start with a visual check for problems that should not be ignored.
steps.warning: Do not apply unapproved lubricants to the post shaft or seals.
steps.check: No obvious damage or unsafe looseness is visible.

steps.title: Cycle the post through its travel
steps.instruction: Operate the remote and move the saddle through the post’s usable travel several times. Observe whether extension and lowering are smooth and repeatable.
steps.why: Intermittent sticking, incomplete return or unexpected movement can indicate a control, pressure or service issue.
steps.check: The post moves predictably through its usable travel.

steps.title: Check remote response
steps.instruction: Confirm that the remote moves freely, returns normally and consistently releases the post mechanism when operated.
steps.why: A sticky or poorly returning remote can make an otherwise healthy post behave inconsistently.
steps.warning: Cable tension, hydraulic controls and electronic systems use different service procedures; follow the actual remote/post manufacturer guidance.
steps.check: Remote actuation is consistent and returns normally.

steps.title: Confirm the saddle stays where commanded
steps.instruction: With the post extended and then at a lower position, apply normal controlled rider load and confirm it does not unexpectedly sink or extend.
steps.why: The post should hold its selected position until deliberately released.
steps.warning: If the post moves unexpectedly under normal load, stop relying on it until the cause is identified or serviced.
steps.check: The saddle position remains stable until the remote is deliberately operated.
